summary: Record the slot-lifecycle transition idiom (FOR UPDATE) in AGENTS.md
description:
**As** the team, **I want** the catalog slot-lifecycle **transition idiom** recorded in `AGENTS.md`, so US-009/US-011 (and every later slot transition) don't re-introduce the check-then-act race that AI-review caught in TKT-49.

**Priority:** P3
**Depends on:** — (documentation; TKT-49 is Done and is the reference implementation)
**Type:** Task · `risk:low` — a docs-only edit to `AGENTS.md`, no code.

**Background:** In TKT-49, the first archive implementation did a conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE status='published'` and then re-read status in a *separate* statement to decide whether to emit the domain event. A concurrent `draft→publish` could commit in between, producing a phantom `performance.archived` event on a still-published row (with a nil `archived_at` → mismatched deterministic id). Codex adversarial review flagged it [BLOCKING]. The fix: decide **and** transition inside one transaction with the row locked `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` (the same idiom as `services/access/internal/store/postgres.go` redeem). This is a promotable **technical learning** (metrics comment on TKT-49, learning #1) routed through a gated ticket per the '3 houses' rule rather than committed directly to the shared `AGENTS.md`.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` gains a short note (a line or two, in the working-agreement/conventions area) stating: any catalog slot-lifecycle transition that both mutates state AND derives a to-emit decision must decide under `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` in one transaction; a conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE status=x` followed by a separate re-read is racy and can emit a phantom domain event.
- [ ] The note cites the reference implementations: `catalog ArchivePerformance` and `access` redeem.
- [ ] No code change; `make check` still green (docs-only).

Quality gates: `make check` green (docs-only, so trivially); no contract/UI surface.

binding.rule: Every admission-granting offer (performance, festival day, park operating day) is a dated slot in one inventory machinery; passes are entitlements to claim slot entries; lodging/day resources reserve through the same contention-safe core; slot attributes carry domain specifics — the claim primitive does not fork.

reference.summary: TKT-49 metrics comment — learning #1 (the promotable transition idiom); reference impl catalog ArchivePerformance + access redeem
PRD v1 — TKT-2 catalog stories (US-009/US-011 will add more slot transitions)
